Regard now, as a sensible physiologist, the Sperm Whale’s front in its compacted collectedness; form an unexaggerated estimate of whatever battering-ram power is lodged there. Here is a vital point; for you must either satisfactorily settle this matter with yourself, or for ever remain an infidel as to one of the most appalling, but not the less true events, perhaps anywhere to be found in all recorded history. In ordinary swimming the front presents an almost wholly vertical plane; mouth entirely under the head; no external nose—the spout-hole on top; eyes and ears set far back at the sides. The whole front is a dead, blind wall, without organ or tender prominence. Bone does not begin till near twenty feet from the forehead; all before is an enormous boneless wad. About the head the blubber, though not so thick, is of a boneless toughness; the severest harpoon, the sharpest lance, impotently rebounds from it—as though the forehead were paved with horses’ hoofs. I do not think that any sensation lurks in it.

Think of sailors fending two crowding Indiamen: not iron or wood, but a large wad of tow and cork in ox-hide takes the jam. Ordinary fish possess what is called a swimming-bladder; the Sperm Whale, as far as I know, has none; yet he now depresses his head altogether beneath the surface, anon swims with it high elevated. Considering the honeycombed interior and the unobstructed elasticity of its envelope, those mystical lung-celled honeycombs may possibly have some unsuspected connexion with the outer air, to be susceptible to atmospheric distension and contraction. If this be so, fancy the irresistibleness of that might, to which the most impalpable and destructive of all elements contributes. Now, mark. Unerringly impelling this dead, impregnable, uninjurable wall, and this most buoyant thing within; there swims behind it all a mass of tremendous life, only to be adequately estimated as piled wood is—by the cord; and all obedient to one volition, as the smallest insect.

So that when I shall hereafter detail his more inconsiderable braining feats, be ready to abide by this: that though the Sperm Whale stove a passage through the Isthmus of Darien, and mixed the Atlantic with the Pacific, you would not elevate one hair of your eye-brow. For unless you own the whale, you are but a provincial and sentimentalist in Truth. But clear Truth is a thing for salamander giants only to encounter; how small the chances for the provincials then? What befell the weakling youth lifting the dread goddess’s veil at Lais?
